page: Amazon Web Services m6id.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors. The system delivers 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs running at 3.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, paired with 54 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-level virtualization (VMX) is directly accessible without hypervisor overhead, alongside specialized vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI.

Integrated local storage is provided via 7,600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store capacity, addressing high-throughput, low-latency requirements without routing data through network-attached storage. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The server operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on the host CPU for all compute workloads.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-threaded and memory-intensive throughput. In stress-ng, multi-core CPU performance reached 125,020.56, placing it in the top 25% bracket, while single-core performance registered 1,909.88 in the middle 50%. The PassMark CPU test yielded 87,921.99, boosted by strong results in cryptographic routines (113,057.93) and extended instruction sets (108,757.11). Memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrated uncached large-block read bandwidth of 339.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 133.21 GB/sec.

Application-level performance tests reflect high concurrent execution capacity, with Redis SET throughput achieving 111.37 million operations per second and static web serving throughput hitting 73.53 GB/sec. Large-scale software builds via Clang registered 53,730.0 in Geekbench. CPU-driven LLM inference delivers strong prompt processing throughput across small and medium models, though token generation speeds remain moderate due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density by packing 128 dedicated compute threads, 512 GB of RAM, and fast local NVMe storage into a single bare-metal deployment. This design suits relational database clusters, large Redis caching tiers, continuous integration build farms, container hosts, and transactional enterprise workloads that need high NVMe IOPS and high network throughput without virtualization penalties.
